title: What does SponsorshipSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of SponsorshipSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, SponsorshipSet configures a ledger sponsorship relationship that can cover another account's transaction fees or reserves. [1]

The documented Sponsor feature separates a sponsor's financial commitment from the beneficiary's transaction authority. Fee and reserve sponsorship have different controls. Inspect the sponsorship settings and signer requirements before treating a third party's balance as available for an operation; an agreement to sponsor does not authorize arbitrary spending. [1]

The SponsorshipSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using SponsorshipSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
